jobs.description:
JOB DESCRIPTION
At eBay, we're more than a global ecommerce leader — we’re changing the way the world shops and sells. Our platform empowers millions of buyers and sellers in more than 190 markets around the world. We’re committed to pushing boundaries and leaving our mark as we reinvent the future of ecommerce for enthusiasts.


Our customers are our compass, authenticity thrives, bold ideas are welcome, and everyone can bring their unique selves to work — every day. We're in this together, sustaining the future of our customers, our company, and our planet.


Join a team of passionate thinkers, innovators, and dreamers — and help us connect people and build communities to create economic opportunity for all.


eBay is a global marketplace connecting millions of buyers and sellers across more than 190 markets. People come to eBay to discover unique and pre\-loved goods, pursue their interests, and grow businesses. Our purpose is to connect people and build communities to create economic opportunity for all.

  

  

**About the team and the role**


Low Cost Shipping is a key strategic initiative focused on delivering a more affordable, competitive, and sustainable shipping experience for eBay and Depop customers. By employing lower shipping costs to offer compelling customer pricing, the initiative aims to drive adoption, influence customer behavior, and unlock new growth opportunities, all while strengthening operational efficiency and long\-term unit economics.

  

  

This role leads the economic architecture of the low cost shipping business. You will own the business recommendation on pricing, subsidy, unit economics, contribution, and the economic conditions required to launch, expand, or change course.

  

  

The role sits at the intersection of customer behavior and physical network economics: understanding how cost changes with parcel flow and density, how buyers and sellers respond to price, and whether lower shipping prices create incremental marketplace activity rather than simply subsidizing existing transactions.

  

  

**What you will accomplish**


* Manage the end\-to\-end economic model for low cost shipping, including partner rates, network costs, buyer pricing, subsidy, contribution, and fixed and variable investment
* Understand economics at the level that decisions are actually made: by market, parcel flow, customer cohort, partner, and network stage rather than relying on blended averages
* Define buyer\-facing pricing and subsidy recommendations that balance adoption, incrementality, contribution economics, and the long\-term path to structurally lower shipping cost
* Establish the economic thresholds that determine when the business should STOP, SLOW, or EXPAND, including break\-even volume, density, utilization, and subsidy requirements
* Develop a deep understanding of price sensitivity, incrementality, cohort response, and experiment outcomes; continuously update the economic thesis as customer behavior becomes observable
* Distinguish incremental marketplace value from shipment substitution. Determine whether pricing changes are creating incremental conversion, frequency, GMV, or low\-ASP TAM rather than simply moving existing volume or buying adoption
* Build scenarios and sensitivities that show how partner rates, flow mix, density, node utilization, customer behavior, and network design change the economics and required investment
* Translate the analysis into clear business recommendations for senior leaders on pricing, investment, network expansion, partner economics, and market sequencing
  

  

**What you will bring**


* Deep quantitative fluency and the ability to personally work through complex financial, operational, customer, and network data rather than relying solely on prepared analysis. SQL or equivalent analytical capability is strongly preferred.
* Strong understanding of pricing, elasticity, experimentation, incrementality, unit economics, contribution economics, and sensitivity analysis
* Experience building economic models where customer behavior and cost structure interact — ideally in marketplaces, logistics, transportation, consumer pricing, or another network business
* Ability to distinguish correlation from causality and design or interpret experiments that can support pricing and investment decisions
* Strong commercial judgment: able to translate detailed analysis into a recommendation, identify the few assumptions that actually drive the answer, and state what evidence would change the recommendation
* Ability to challenge partner cost structures, operating assumptions, forecasts, and internally generated business cases rather than treating supplied inputs as fixed
* Demonstrated ability to influence Finance, Product, Analytics, Growth, Operations, and senior leadership without direct authority
* Bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience; advanced quantitative training is useful but not required
  

  

**How we will measure success**


Success means we can answer, with increasing confidence: what does each parcel flow actually cost, what customer price changes behavior, how much subsidy is required, how much demand is incremental, and at what volume and density the network becomes structurally advantaged.

  

  

The role succeeds when better economics allow us to sustainably lower customer shipping prices and unlock incremental marketplace activity — not simply when low cost shipping volume increases or the modeled P\&L improves.

GreenShield is a proudly Canadian, national non\-profit health care and insurance organization, driven by our mission of Better Health for All. Through GreenShield Cares, we positively impacted the health and well\-being of over one million Canadians between 2020 and 2025\. What’s driving us now is the commitment to measurably impact an additional three million Canadians by 2030 – across mental health, essential medicines, and chronic disease management – through scalable initiatives that deliver meaningful change in pursuit of our mission of Better Health for All.

This leader will bring the discipline to maintain a strong third line of defence and the pragmatism to ensure Internal Audit Services remains relevant as GreenShield’s strategy, operating model and risk environment continue to evolve.

* Provide independent assurance to the Board and Audit Committee on the effectiveness of governance, enterprise risk management and internal controls.
* Ensure audit coverage addresses risks across GreenShield’s payer and provider businesses and the connections between them. Coverage includes technology, cyber, data and AI, privacy, regulatory, third\-party, partnership and operational resilience risks.

* Build and lead a skilled, diverse and high\-performing team, developing the capabilities required to address current and emerging enterprise risks and drawing on specialized expertise where needed.

* 10\+ years of progressive internal audit, risk, assurance or related experience, including significant leadership responsibility and at least five years leading people.

ABOUT SAPA CANADA

  

SAPA Canada is an independent Canadian charity that works alongside the Sudanese American Physicians Association (SAPA) to fund its work. SAPA is a physician\-led humanitarian organization that in 2025 treated 750,000 patients and served 3\.1 million meals in Sudan, Chad and Uganda, in the places most other organizations have left. Every SAPA site is run by Sudanese doctors, nurses and volunteers, nearly 2,000 of them, working in their own country under fire.

  

SAPA Canada has its own board, its own governance and its own charitable registration. It sets its own direction in Canada and chooses what it funds; its support reaches SAPA's hospitals, clinics and kitchens through funding agreements that SAPA Canada's board approves. It is in its first full year of operation, with a Year 1 operating budget approved, a growing Canadian donor base, and a Toronto/GTA Community Partnerships \& Fundraising Officer being recruited now.

  

The Executive Director leads SAPA Canada alongside a senior role in SAPA's global team. This hire is the person who runs SAPA Canada day to day: the organization needs someone whose whole job it is.

  

THE ROLE

  

The Director of Operations \& Development is SAPA Canada's most senior staff member and runs the organization day to day. You report to the Executive Director and work closely with the SAPA Canada board.

  

You own two things: that SAPA Canada is run properly as a Canadian charity (compliance, finance, governance, systems), and that it raises money in Canada (donors, campaigns, grants, and the community fundraising program). You will be the first person in this seat, so you build much of it: policies, processes, the donor pipeline, the reporting rhythm.

  

This is a builder's role in a small organization with a large mission behind it. The programs SAPA Canada funds are already running at scale; your job is to grow the Canadian side so it can fund more of them.

  

WHAT YOU WILL DO

  

Run the charity


* Own CRA compliance end to end: T3010 annual return, official donation receipts, books and records, disbursement rules, and the reporting that comes with funding programs outside Canada.


* Manage finance with the bookkeeper and auditor: monthly close, cash flow, the Year 1 budget and the Year 2 budget you will build, grant and funding\-agreement reconciliation, and audited statements.


* Put the operating backbone in place: financial and HR policies, insurance, banking, donor database (Salesforce, shared with SAPA), document management and the systems a growing team needs.


* Draft and administer the funding agreements through which SAPA Canada funds SAPA programs, and the reporting that goes back to Canadian donors on how their money was used.

  

Raise money in Canada


* Build and run SAPA Canada's annual fundraising plan: individual giving, monthly donors, Ramadan and year\-end campaigns, and the stewardship that keeps donors giving.


* Manage the Toronto/GTA Community Partnerships \& Fundraising Officer and, as the team grows, further officers in other Canadian cities.


* Open institutional funding: foundations, corporate partners, and government programs where SAPA Canada is eligible.


* Hold a portfolio of major and mid\-level Canadian donors yourself, with the Executive Director on the largest relationships.


* Report monthly to the Executive Director and quarterly to the board on funds raised, pipeline, costs and what is planned.

  

Governance and the board


* Serve as board secretariat: agendas, papers, minutes, resolutions, filings, and the annual general meeting.


* Keep the board's compliance calendar and make sure every filing, renewal and policy review happens on time.


* Support the Executive Director in board recruitment and orientation.

  

Lead the team


* Recruit, manage and develop SAPA Canada staff and contractors as the organization grows.


* Work with SAPA's Global Communications \& Fundraising team on brand, campaigns, content and the donor database, so Canadian donors get the same quality of communication as everyone else and SAPA Canada never duplicates work that already exists.


* Represent SAPA Canada with partners, donors, sector bodies and government when the Executive Director does not.

  

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE IN YEAR ONE

  

Targets are agreed with you in your first 60 days. What we expect to see:


* 90 days: you know the books, the filings and the donor base; the compliance calendar exists; the Toronto/GTA Officer is onboarded and in market; a Ramadan 2027 plan is ready.


* Ramadan (Feb 8 to Mar 9, 2027\): SAPA Canada's first full Ramadan campaign delivered, online and in person, with every donor receipted and thanked within the month.


* 6 months: monthly financial close running on time; a Year 2 budget in front of the board; first institutional funding applications submitted; funding agreements with SAPA in place and reported on.


* 12 months: T3010 filed and audit clean; a growing monthly\-donor base; a documented donor journey from first gift to major gift; a second Canadian market scoped; and an organization that runs for a month without the Executive Director in the room.

  

WHO WE ARE LOOKING FOR

  

Someone who has run a Canadian charity, or a significant part of one, and wants to build the next one from the ground up for Sudan.

**About Innerlogic**

Most organizations survey their people, then wait months for the analysis. By the time the report lands, the moment to act has often passed. Innerlogic closes that gap.

We’re an employee listening platform with an agentic twist. Teams run engagement, pulse and 360 surveys on Innerlogic, and Nora, our AI analyst, turns the results into reports, insights and action plans in minutes. Enterprises use us to listen across their whole workforce. HR consultancies use us to run research for many clients at once.

Qualtrics and Culture Amp were built for a world where analysis took a team and a quarter. We’re building for one where it takes an afternoon.

We’ve just closed a funding round, moved into a new Bedford office, and are putting our full weight behind go\-to\-market. We’re a team of 8, and you’ll be our first marketing leader: the person who decides how the world hears about us.

**The role**

You’ll own the top of our funnel: who knows about us, why they care, and how many qualified conversations reach sales each month.

This is a hands\-on builder’s role. You’ll set the strategy and do much of the work yourself, from writing the positioning to launching the campaigns. You’ll have a budget for contractors and tools from day one, and you’ll decide when and where to grow a team.

We build our product with AI agents, and we expect marketing to run the same way. You’ll use tools like Claude to research markets, draft and test messaging, build campaigns and analyze results, so a small team ships like a much bigger one.

**Location:** This is a hybrid role based in our Bedford office. The team works together in person 2 days a week, so you’ll need to live within commuting distance of Halifax. We can’t consider fully remote candidates for this role.

**What you’ll do**

* **Build pipeline.** Design and run the programs that create qualified pipeline: paid, email nurture, webinars, events, partner campaigns and support for outbound. Own the numbers from first visit to marketing\-sourced pipeline.
* **Sharpen our positioning.** Define how we talk about Innerlogic against Qualtrics, Culture Amp and the rest. Own launches, messaging, sales collateral, competitive battlecards and pricing pages.
* **Market to two audiences.** Build distinct plays for HR and People leaders who buy directly, and for HR consultancies who run research on our platform.
* **Run a content engine.** Publish work that earns attention: research reports from our own data, blog, SEO and AI\-search visibility, LinkedIn and customer stories.
* **Own the brand and website.** Steward the brand and run the website as a conversion engine, working with product on design.
* **Run marketing operations.** Own the CRM and marketing automation setup, lead scoring, attribution and reporting, so we always know what’s working.

**Your first 90 days**

* Learn the product, our customers, and the deals we’ve won and lost. Talk to customers and consultancy partners.
* Deliver a positioning refresh and a 12\-month marketing plan with targets and budget.
* Launch the first repeatable pipeline program, and the reporting to measure it.

**What you bring**

* 7\+ years in B2B marketing, ideally SaaS, including at least 2 years owning demand generation or the whole marketing function at an early\-stage company.
* A track record of building pipeline from little or nothing, with the numbers to show for it.
* Excellent writing. You can produce a sharp landing page, email or one\-pager yourself.
* Product marketing instincts: you can turn a technical product into a clear story for a specific buyer.
* Comfort with data and modern tools. You run your own CRM, automation and analytics, build your own dashboards and make budget calls from them.
* You already work AI\-first. You use tools like Claude to research, write, analyze and automate, and you can walk us through a workflow you built that changed your output.
* Range. You’re happy moving from strategy to a campaign launch to fixing a form in the same day.

**Nice to have**

* Experience marketing to HR, People or employee experience buyers.
* Partner or channel marketing experience.
* HubSpot experience.
* Experience marketing an AI product.

**What we offer**

* $115,000–$135,000 CAD base salary, plus a meaningful stock option grant vesting over time.
* A real budget for programs, tools and contractors.
* Direct influence on company strategy, working alongside the founders.
* Hybrid work from our new Bedford office.
* A clear path to VP Marketing as the team grows.

**How we hire**

A short intro call, conversations with our founders and the team, and a small practical exercise. We’ll walk you through the details on the first call.

**How to apply**

Apply through Indeed with your resume and a short note on a pipeline program you built: what you did and what it produced. Links to work you wrote or launched are welcome. We review applications as they arrive and aim to have someone in the role by early 2027\.

Innerlogic welcomes applicants of all backgrounds. If you need an accommodation at any stage of the hiring process, tell us and we’ll work with you.

Pay: $115,000\.00\-$135,000\.00 per year

Work Location: Hybrid remote in Bedford, NS B4A 4J4
